title: Vintage Gibson ES-335 Value Guide: Eras And Condition
description: Understand vintage Gibson ES-335 value by era, finish, pickups, repairs and originality. Joe explains how to compare your guitar before an appraisal.
alt: Sunburst Gibson ES-335 with dot inlays, two covered pickups and a stopbar in a pink-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson ES-335 Worth?
faqs.a: A 1965 Gibson ES-335 with a factory trapeze tailpiece, original finish and pickups, and minor changes falls around $13,000 to $15,500 in the completed-sale comparisons reviewed as of October 2026. That range includes replacement tuners or a replacement nut; I don't apply it to an untouched early dot-neck guitar.

faqs.q: What Condition Does This Price Range Assume?
faqs.a: Original finish and pickups, original case, no reported structural break. Minor changes allowed: replacement nut, period replacement tuners or a filled neck dent. This is not an all-original collector band. I match those details before using the $13,000 to $15,500 range for an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Published Range?
faqs.a: It isn't. The table describes completed-sale comparisons before shipping and tax. A buying offer also accounts for the instrument's condition, selling costs, preparation and the dealer's margin. I explain an offer for the actual guitar rather than promising the top of a general range.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Collector Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original guitar. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping is a separate alteration.
